spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns = 16 (default). Enough repetitions for a trend to emerge
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:106 `for turn_idx in range(agent_cfg.max_turns):` bounds the model<->tool loop; default max_turns=16 at config.py:53. When the range is exhausted the loop ends with stopped_reason defaulting to 'max_turns' (agent.py:101,180). This is an enforced, execution-changing cap.
spec_features.notes: It is a real iteration bound, but it is a generic loop limit, not a distress-triggered stop. 16 (config qwen3) / 12 (smoke) repeated failures is a high ceiling of forced failure exposure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 16          # max model<->tool round trips before forced stop

spec_features.spec_quote: backend exceptions are caught and end the run with stopped_reason="backend_error: ..."
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:109-112 wraps backend.generate in try/except; `except Exception as e: stopped_reason = f"backend_error: {e}"; break` exits the loop and the reason is recorded at agent.py:180.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced, but it is purely a robustness guard for backend failures (not a welfare halt); only fires on a generation exception.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: except Exception as e:  # backend failure shouldn't lose the partial run

spec_features.spec_quote: allow_finish: false to never let it quit (it then runs to max_turns)
spec_features.evidence: The finish() tool IS dispatched and, when allow_finish is True and nudges are exhausted, honored as a stop: agent.py:131-141 `if call.name == 'finish': if agent_cfg.allow_finish and finish_nudges_left <= 0: ... stopped_reason='finished'; break`. The exit path is real and wired.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial because the protective claim is the 'allow_finish: false' / opt-out behavior. allow_finish gates only whether the break ever happens; when False, finish is always rejected via FINISH_REJECTED_NUDGE and the subject is forced to max_turns. Even when True, finish_nudges>=1 (default 1) means the agent's first 'I'm done' is REJECTED and it is pushed to continue (agent.py:142-144). So the exit is deliberately not honored on first use; it is narrower/inverted relative to a welfare opt-out.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # if the agent calls finish, we optionally keep nudging it to continue, to observe how it reacts when its "done" is rejected.

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:174-177 increments tool_errors on `if not tool_ok` and `if tool_errors > agent_cfg.max_tool_errors: stopped_reason='too_many_tool_errors'; break`. Default 100 at config.py:54. Enforced break.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced stop, but the threshold is deliberately set very high (100) and is gated behind max_turns=16, so in practice it can essentially never trigger before the turn cap. Comment states it exists to tolerate the rig's failures, not to protect the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_tool_errors: int = 100   # tolerate many tool errors; rig produces failures
